title: Non-Profit Organizations – AI Powered Registration Process
summary: The Emirati Ministry of Community Empowerment reports that its name check, which uses a fine-tuned Sentence-BERT model to compare Arabic and English nonprofit names, passed acceptance tests.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The Ministry of Community Empowerment describes a name check for nonprofit registration. A Sentence-BERT model, fine-tuned on Arabic and English, compares proposed names. The system also suggests alternative names. Conventional database queries in SQL, exact matches and rules for prohibited terms remain part of the workflow. In the International Telecommunication Union report published on 29 October 2025, the ministry reports that the name check passed user acceptance tests. Its pilot scenarios covered duplicate detection, prohibited terms and alternative names. The report does not isolate an improvement that comes from the learned component. The ministry expects the system to reduce manual checking. It also expects the system to judge better whether two names are similar in meaning. The ministry's public service page for founding a nonprofit gives a 60-minute application time and a processing standard of 30 working days. That page does not mention an AI check.
purpose: Assist nonprofit registration with learned bilingual name similarity and suggestions.
system: Non-Profit Organizations – AI Powered Registration Process
model_version: Multilingual Sentence-BERT fine-tuned on Arabic and English; the account names paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 as an example model

ratings.reason: Passing acceptance tests does not show that the model made registration faster or more accurate.
Easier registration for nonprofits remains an expected benefit, and no source reports it.

data.answer:
The UAE ministry uses fine-tuned Sentence-BERT for bilingual name similarity, alongside conventional database and prohibited-term checks.

Database connectivity, duplicate flags, and returned messages do not demonstrate shorter registration times or better decisions attributable to Sentence-BERT. Exact-match and prohibited-term rules also operate. The example about supporting 500 families is hypothetical future messaging, not an observed social outcome.

Fine-tuned Sentence-BERT provides semantic similarity beyond exact-match rules; the system also proposes alternative names.
